forecast.event: initial seasonally adjusted jobless claims for week ending 2026-08-15 are >=220000

benchmarks.name: neutral_binary
benchmarks.note: Protocol comparator only; not claimed to be the strongest empirical base-rate benchmark for the >=220k event.

benchmarks.name: latest_observation_no_change
benchmarks.note: Initial claims for week ending 2026-08-08 reported on Aug. 13; fixed as the point no-change benchmark.

original_forecast.resolution_rule: Use the first U.S. Department of Labor weekly unemployment-insurance release published 2026-08-20. Resolve the binary event TRUE if seasonally adjusted initial claims for the week ending 2026-08-15 are 220,000 or higher, otherwise FALSE. Score Brier and log loss. Score the 211,000 point estimate by absolute error versus the same first-release value and record whether the 80% interval covers. Do not substitute later revisions unless the Department of Labor corrects the initial release before scoring.
rationale: The latest verified claims reading was 209,000, so low layoffs still argue against an already broad H002 contraction despite July payroll, retail, consumer-goods, and housing weakness.

July housing and consumer-goods weakness create a prospective transmission risk into layoffs; a rise to >=220,000 would be a materially more discriminating H002 confirmation than another aggregate equity-price move.
Positive July industrial production and tight latest-verified credit spreads prevent assigning a high probability to a claims jump, so the event is forecast below even at 0.36.
The forecast is intentionally tied to the first release so subsequent revisions cannot be used for hindsight adjustment.
surprising_if: Claims are >=240,000, indicating a much faster transmission from household-side weakness into layoffs than the current model expects.
Claims remain below 200,000 while housing/consumer weakness persists, strengthening the low-churn soft-landing interpretation and weakening near-term H002 transmission.

resolution.source: U.S. Department of Labor first weekly claims release for the week ending 2026-08-15, contemporaneously reported by Reuters on 2026-08-20: initial seasonally adjusted claims 206,000; prior week revised to 212,000. Continued claims for the week ending 2026-08-08 were 1.799 million.
resolution.audit_note: Forecast content above is preserved without hindsight alteration. The >=220,000 event resolved FALSE at 206,000. The 0.36 event probability earned a favorable proper score versus the neutral binary comparator, but the 211,000 point estimate lost to the frozen 209,000 no-change point benchmark (5,000 vs 3,000 absolute error). This result therefore supports the forecast's low-probability layoff-jump assessment without establishing point-forecast skill or broad soft-landing validity. Scored before post-cutoff evidence was used for model revision.
